question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s consolidated control over the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced by ongoing high-level purges in the military and elite ranks, underpins the 95% trader consensus that he will remain in office through the end of 2026. At 73, he shows no public signs of retirement and has avoided naming a successor, with analysts across multiple reports anticipating a fourth term at the 21st Party Congress in late 2027. Institutional norms such as age limits have been selectively applied or bypassed under his leadership, and recent activities—including military parades and diplomatic engagements—signal continuity rather than transition. While a sudden health crisis or unforeseen elite realignment could theoretically alter the timeline, the absence of visible internal challenges or succession mechanisms makes early departure before 2027 highly improbable in the current environment.
